title: The Expulsion of Banu al-Nadir
subtitle: Breach of Covenant, Fortress Siege, and Surah Al-Hashr
summary: The treaty blood-money dispute, the rooftop assassination conspiracy against the Prophet, the unfulfilled promises of the hypocrites, the siege of the stone fortresses, and the divine revelation of Surah Al-Hashr regulating the property of Fay'.

sections.text: The Blood Money & The Treaty Obligation

In the aftermath of the Bi'r Ma'una tragedy, Amr ibn Umayyah al-Damri was the sole Muslim survivor to escape captivity. While returning along the highway to Madinah, he encountered two travelers from the Banu Amir tribe sleeping under the shade of a tree. Unaware that the Prophet ﷺ had previously granted these individuals a solemn covenant of protection, Amr killed them in retaliation for his fallen brethren at the well. Upon arriving in Madinah, he reported his deed. The Prophet ﷺ immediately disapproved and declared: 'You have slain two men for whom I must certainly pay full blood money (diya)!'

Under the terms of the Constitution of Madinah (Sahifat al-Madinah), the Jewish tribe of Banu al-Nadir was in mutual alliance with both the Muslims and the Banu Amir, and was treaty-bound to contribute to communal blood-money payments. Accompanied by a small escort including Abu Bakr, Umar, and Ali, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ walked to the fortified settlements of Banu al-Nadir on the outskirts of Madinah to request their customary contribution.

The elders of Banu al-Nadir received the Prophet ﷺ courteously on the surface, seating him against the wall of one of their high stone houses and promising to collect the funds. However, behind closed doors, their leaders—including Huyayy ibn Akhtab—conspired to commit an act of irreversible treachery. They argued among themselves: 'You will never find him in such a vulnerable position again! Who among you will climb to the top of this wall and cast down a heavy millstone upon his head, ridding us of him forever?' A man named Amr ibn Jihash volunteered to execute the assassination.

Before the plot could be enacted, divine revelation reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, disclosing the lethal conspiracy. Without betraying alarm, the Prophet ﷺ quietly rose from his seat as if attending to an urgent errand and walked swiftly back to Madinah. His companions, realizing after some time that he had not returned, hurried after him. When they found him at the Prophet's Mosque, he informed them of the attempted assassination and the complete dissolution of the treaty.

The Prophet ﷺ dispatched Muhammad ibn Maslamah, a chief of the Aws who had traditional ties with Banu al-Nadir, to deliver a clear ultimatum: 'The Messenger of Allah has sent me to you: depart from this city within ten days, for you have broken your covenant and plotted murder. Whoever among you is found here after ten days shall be put to the sword.' Banu al-Nadir initially prepared their pack-animals to leave peaceably.

At that critical moment, Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, the leader of the hypocrites, sent a secret delegation urging them to hold their ground. He declared: 'Do not abandon your homes and wealth! Stay inside your strongholds, for I have two thousand warriors from my people ready to defend you, and the Banu Qurayza will come to your aid. If you are fought, we shall fight beside you, and if you are expelled, we will depart with you.' Deceived by these empty assurances, Huyayy ibn Akhtab sent a defiant message to the Prophet ﷺ: 'We will not leave our lands; do whatever you wish.'
The Fortress Siege & The Descent of Surah Al-Hashr

The Prophet ﷺ proclaimed 'Allahu Akbar!' and mobilized the Muslim army. They surrounded the massive stone strongholds of Banu al-Nadir, cutting off their access to water and the surrounding date-palm groves. Day after day passed, yet the promised reinforcements from Abdullah ibn Ubayy never materialized. As the Qur'an vividly recounts in Surah Al-Hashr, the hypocrites were like Satan, who urges man to disbelieve, only to abandon him when calamity strikes.

To break their defensive obstinacy, the Prophet ﷺ ordered the cutting and burning of a specific section of their date-palm trees known as 'al-Linah' (soft, sweet date palms). Banu al-Nadir shouted from the ramparts, accusing him of spreading corruption, but divine revelation immediately confirmed the strategic legitimacy of the action:

مَا قَطَعْتُم مِّن لِّينَةٍ أَوْ تَرَكْتُمُوهَا قَائِمَةً عَلَىٰ أُصُولِهَا فَبِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ وَلِيُخْزِيَ الْفَاسِقِينَ
'Whatever palm-trees you cut down or left standing upon their roots—it was by permission of Allah, and so that He might disgrace the defiantly disobedient.' (Surah Al-Hashr 59:5)
The Capitulation & The Distribution of Fay'

When they asked to leave, the Prophet allowed them to depart with their families and what their camels could carry, except weapons and armor. The classical sirah says they took the timber of their houses and left in a large convoy, most of them for Khaybar. A figure of six hundred camels is part of that biographical account. It is not a number in the Bukhari reports cited here, and this chapter does not treat it as one.

Because the fortresses were yielded without active cavalry engagement, the captured lands and weaponry were classified not as standard spoils of war (Ghanimah), but as Fay'—communal state assets under the Prophet's sole discretion. The Prophet ﷺ allocated these lands exclusively to the impoverished Muhajirun, freeing them from financial dependency on the generous Ansar, and establishing permanent economic stability for the Muslim state.
